name: Brugia malayi

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Stained microfilaria: approximately 175–230 µm, sheathed, with separated terminal and subterminal nuclei near the tail tip.
Adults inhabit lymphatics; apparent size and sheath staining vary with preparation.

transmission.detail: Mosquito-transmitted larvae mature in lymphatics; microfilariae circulate and are ingested by mosquitoes.

life_cycle.detail: Mosquito-transmitted larvae mature in lymphatics; microfilariae circulate and are ingested by mosquitoes.
Microfilariae in peripheral blood; collect with local periodicity and laboratory guidance in mind.

hosts: Definitive: humans; animal reservoirs occur in some systems. Intermediate/vector: mosquitoes, including Mansonia in relevant settings.
distribution: Focal South and Southeast Asian distribution; historical Thai transmission must be distinguished from current surveillance findings.
clinical_significance: Lymphatic filariasis with inflammatory episodes and chronic limb lymphedema.
specimen: Microfilariae in peripheral blood; collect with local periodicity and laboratory guidance in mind.
diagnostics: Stained blood films or concentration; inspect full head/tail and use molecular support where needed.
differential_diagnosis: Differentiate from W. bancrofti using tail nuclei and body features together; folded or clipped tails should remain indeterminate.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Brugia malayi — Malayan lymphatic filaria. Lymphatic filariasis with inflammatory episodes and chronic limb lymphedema.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
Separate thick and thin films; retain erythrocyte context for malaria and full head/tail context for microfilariae.
